text: dsh-plugin-ponytail 为 DSH Web 提供项目级开发规则与技能。它通过 systemPrompt.context 加载规则，从 .ponytail/skills/ 提供技能，并以 /ponytail 命令切换 lite、full、ultra、off 模式或查看状态。插件从会话目录向上查找 .ponytail/，并将模式写入项目 state 文件，适合希望按项目调整开发指导的 DSH 用户。

dsh-plugin-ponytail brings project coding rules and skills to DSH Web. It loads rules through systemPrompt.context, serves .ponytail/skills/, and offers /ponytail to change modes or view status. It finds .ponytail/ above the session and saves the mode in the project state file.
我想让 DSH 根据当前项目自动加载开发规则。
怎么在 DSH 里按项目切换编码规范的严格程度？
I want DSH to load project-specific coding guidance and skills from a directory.
dsh-plugin-ponytail 的功能「项目规则」：向上查找 .ponytail/，按 state 级别把规则加入 DSH 上下文；off 时停止注入。
dsh-plugin-ponytail 的功能「模式命令」：使用 /ponytail 查看或切换项目级别，并可保存默认值到用户配置。

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · dsh-plugin-ponytail：[ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail) — "lazy senior dev mode" —
as a native [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
plugin.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · dsh-plugin-ponytail：Upstream ponytail ships adapters for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kiro,
Windsurf and others, and none for DSH: its always-on layer is a `UserPromptSubmit`
lifecycle hook, which DSH agents do not have. This package rebuilds that layer on
the DSH extension points that do exist, so you get the reference behaviour without
patching upstream and without planting generated files in your repositories.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · What it contributes：| Contribution | DSH extension point |
|---|---|
| The always-on rules, recomputed for every prompt | `systemPrompt.context()` |
| The six `ponytail*` skills, listed only while the mode is on | `skills.registerProvider()` |
| `/ponytail lite\|full\|ultra\|off\|status` | `commands.register()` |

Nothing is written into your project: no `AGENTS.local.md`, no symlinks in
`.agents/skills`. The only artifact is the `.ponytail/` directory you already have.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins：- [`dsh-ponytail`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-ponytail) (ccll) vendors
  `@dietrichgebert/ponytail` as a dependency, injects the ruleset as a **global
  system-prompt section** (reaching subagents too), adds the six skills as runtime
  skills, and detects the "stop ponytail" / "normal mode" deactivation. Global and
  per-session.
- [`dsh-ponytail-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-ponytail-skills)
  (gongyijie85, repository `gongyijie85/dsh-ponytail`) ships the six skills inside
  the package and registers only a `ctx.skills` provider. **Skills only**: it
  injects no rules, so the style is adopted when the model chooses to load the
  skill rather than being enforced on every prompt.
- This package: always-on rules **plus** skills **plus** the command, scoped to a
  project by the presence of `.ponytail/`.
section: Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins：|  | `dsh-ponytail` | `dsh-ponytail-skills` | this package |
|---|---|---|---|
| Always-on rules | yes (system-prompt section) | no | yes (runtime context, or a section) |
| Skills | 6, registered at mount | 6, provider from the package | whatever is in `.ponytail/skills/` |
| `/ponytail` command | yes | no | yes |
| Deactivation gesture | yes | no | yes |
| Which projects get it | all | all | only those with a `.ponytail/` above the cwd |
| Mode storage | in-process, per session | n/a | `.ponytail/state`, on disk, per project |
| Mode after resuming a session | back to the default | n/a | preserved |
| Upstream text | `require`d at runtime | shipped in the package | vendored into `.ponytail/` by your own tooling |
| Name/invocation frontmatter rules | n/a | follows the built-in provider | follows the built-in provider |

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins：Ideas borrowed from `dsh-ponytail`, because they were right: optional per-feature
injection instead of a hard `inject` (a profile without a command surface must not
lose the rules), loud rejection of unknown config keys, the whole-message
deactivation gesture, a `/ponytail default` command, and shipped types.
section: Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins

text:
dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins：Ideas taken from `dsh-ponytail-skills`: honouring the built-in provider's
frontmatter contract — the `disable-model-invocation` / `user-invocable` invocation
policy and the kebab-case name grammar, so a skill placed in `.ponytail/skills/`
behaves exactly as it would in `.agents/skills/`.
section: Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins

text:
dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins：Ideas this package contributes: per-project opt-in by walking up from the cwd
(which crosses nested repository roots), mode state on disk so it survives resume
and restart, and `systemPrompt.context` as the default placement so a level change
does not perturb the system-prompt prefix.

Install any one of them, not two: `dsh-ponytail` and this package each register a
`/ponytail` command, and the second registration fails.
section: Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins

text:
dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Relationship to the other DSH ponytail plugins：If you want ponytail everywhere with no per-project setup, use `dsh-ponytail`. If
you only want the skills available and are happy for the model to decide when to
use them, `dsh-ponytail-skills` is the smaller install. If you want to opt in per
project, enforce the rules on every prompt, and keep the mode next to the code,
use this.

text:
dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-ponytail
```

The manifest declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the package also joins
`dsh.profile.bundles` and the loader applies its patch as one more layer. Restart
the profile so the new layer boots.

For a checkout instead of the registry:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-plugin-ponytail
```

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Mounting into a running host：DSH reads `dsh.profile.bundles` from the profile's `package.json` at boot, so a
bundle normally takes effect on the next start. A profile with
`patchReload: live` does watch its patch files continuously, so a running host can
pick the row up without a restart. Leave the package in `dependencies`, remove it
from `dsh.profile.bundles`, and add a pure insert to the profile's own patch layer
(`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Mounting into a running host：```yaml
- insert:
    - id: ponytail
      name: dsh-plugin-ponytail
```

Keep it out of `dsh.profile.bundles` while that insert exists.
`applyEntryPatches` does not deduplicate inserts by id, so the row would mount
twice — once from the bundle patch and once from the profile layer.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Set up a project：The plugin contributes nothing until it finds a `.ponytail/` directory. Presence is
the opt-in.

```sh
mkdir -p .ponytail/skills

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · state               — off | lite | full | ultra：printf 'full\n' > .ponytail/state
```

Copying upstream's `skills/` and `AGENTS.md` into `.ponytail/` is enough:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail /tmp/ponytail
mkdir -p .ponytail/skills
cp /tmp/ponytail/AGENTS.md .ponytail/rules.md
cp -R /tmp/ponytail/skills/. .ponytail/skills/
printf 'full\n' > .ponytail/state
```

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · state               — off | lite | full | ultra：Skills you add yourself follow the built-in filesystem provider's contract, so they
behave exactly as they would in `.agents/skills/`: `name` must be kebab-case, and
`disable-model-invocation: true` / `user-invocable: false` control who may invoke
them. A skill whose name or invocation frontmatter is invalid is skipped rather
than half-registered.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · How the directory is found：The plugin walks **up** from the session's working directory until it finds
`.ponytail/`, and stops at the filesystem root.

That one rule is the whole scoping model, and it behaves differently from a file
planted in a single project tree:

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · How the directory is found：- A session started in a **nested repository** still finds `.ponytail/`. If the
  tree holding `.ponytail/` contains a checkout that is itself a git repository, a
  session started inside that checkout is covered too, because the walk crosses
  project roots instead of stopping at the nearest one.
- Every descendant directory inherits the mode, with no per-project installation.
- Sibling projects are unaffected: no `.ponytail/` above them means no rules and no
  skills.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Levels：```sh
/ponytail                        # show the current level, directory and skill count
/ponytail lite                   # name the lazier alternative in one line
/ponytail full                   # the ladder enforced (default)
/ponytail ultra                  # YAGNI extremist, deletion before addition

`/ponytail <level>` writes `.ponytail/state`. The rules are recomputed on the next
prompt, so `off` takes effect immediately and nothing has to be regenerated.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Levels：Upstream's whole-message deactivation gesture also works: a message that is exactly
`stop ponytail` or `normal mode` switches that project to `off`. A message that merely
mentions the phrase ("add a normal mode toggle") does not.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Levels：`/ponytail default <mode>` writes upstream's own
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ponytail/config.json` (or `~/.config/ponytail/config.json`,
`%APPDATA%\ponytail\config.json`), which is the same file the reference adapters
and this plugin's own resolution order read. It is the level used when no
`.ponytail/state` exists.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Levels：The level is resolved exactly as upstream resolves it: `PONYTAIL_DEFAULT_MODE`,
then `defaultMode` from that config file, then this row's `defaultMode`, then
`full`. A per-project `.ponytail/state` wins over all of them.

`ponytail-review` is a skill, not a level; `/ponytail review` says so.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · What the model sees：Upstream's own payload, byte for byte:

```
PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: <mode>

<the mode-filtered body of skills/ponytail/SKILL.md>
```

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · What the model sees：`filterSkillBodyForMode` is a faithful port of upstream
`hooks/ponytail-instructions.js`, including its two subtleties: only the intensity
table rows and the *quoted* worked examples are level-specific, and an ordinary
rule bullet whose label happens to start with a level word survives verbatim. When
`skills/ponytail/SKILL.md` is missing, `.ponytail/rules.md` is used instead.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · What the model sees：Verified against upstream on the vendored `SKILL.md`: identical for `lite`, `full`
and `ultra`, modulo a trailing newline.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Context, cache and cost：The rules are recomputed for every prompt, so it is fair to ask whether that
churns the prompt prefix and costs cache hits. Measured:

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Context, cache and cost：- **The system prompt is never touched.** The default `placement: context` is a
  durable user-role snapshot, not a system-prompt section. The cacheable prefix —
  system prompt and tool schemas — contains no ponytail text.
- **The payload is byte-stable.** Rendering the same unchanged files three times,
  including from a fresh mount, produces identical bytes, and it carries no
  timestamp, path, digest, or process id. That is asserted by a test, so a future
  edit cannot quietly make it nondeterministic.
- **An unchanged contribution is not re-sent.** The harness compares the rendered
  runtime context with the snapshot it already holds and emits a message only when
  the text differs; when it does differ, the new one *replaces* the old rather than
  accumulating. Measured on a live 209-step session using this same seam: exactly
  **one** snapshot message.
- **Skill order cannot flap.** This provider reads `readdirSync`, whose order is not
  guaranteed, but `ctx.skills.snapshot()` sorts, and the catalog digest is a hash of
  `[name, description]` pairs only, so neither order nor metadata can trigger a
  re-emit.
- **What it add

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Context, cache and cost：- `/ponytail lite|full|ultra` (or editing `.ponytail/state`) changes it once; the
  prefix up to that point stays cached, so it is one ordinary cache miss.
- `payload: rules` uses `rules.md` (2590 characters) instead of upstream's
  mode-filtered `SKILL.md` body (5228) for about half the always-on text, at the
  cost of the per-level filtering.
- Re-enabling a file-based layer (`bash .ponytail/switch on`) delivers the rules a
  **second** time as workspace instructions, doubling the text.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · The doubled-ruleset warning：That last configuration is the one real trap, so the plugin detects it. When an
`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.local.md`, or `CLAUDE.local.md` anywhere from the
ponytail root down to the session cwd carries an upstream ponytail marker, the
agent is warned in the prompt, and `/ponytail status` reports it:

```
  duplicate : /path/to/AGENTS.local.md — rules also arrive as workspace instructions
```

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · The doubled-ruleset warning：The warning is its own prompt entry, so a healthy project contributes nothing and
the rules payload stays byte-identical to upstream's. It requires an upstream phrase
(`PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE`, "lazy senior dev", "best code is the code never written"),
not merely the word "ponytail", so a project that mentions the name is not flagged.
Set `warnOnDuplicateInstructions: false` to turn it off.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Configuration：The row takes an optional config. Every field is optional.

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: ponytail
      name: dsh-plugin-ponytail
      config:

`placement: section` registers a system-prompt section instead of a runtime
context. Use it only if you need the rules pinned into the system prompt: it
changes the prompt prefix whenever the level changes, and the default `context`
placement is the same durable user-role snapshot shape the harness uses for
workspace instructions.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Caveats：- The `minimal` agent preset calls `suppressRuntimeContext()`, which switches off
  every dynamic context in that scope. With the default `placement: context` the
  rules are silent there; use `placement: section` if you need them on `minimal`.
- A catalog read lists skills but does not load their bodies; each body is read from
  disk when the skill is actually used.
- The plugin serves whatever is in `.ponytail/skills/`. Keeping that directory
  current is upstream's problem, not this package's.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Migrating from a file-based install：If you had ponytail wired through a generated `AGENTS.local.md` plus symlinks in
`.agents/skills/`, turn that layer off and leave `.ponytail/` in place:

```sh
bash .ponytail/switch off # removes AGENTS.local.md and the symlinks
```

The plugin reads the same `.ponytail/rules.md`, `.ponytail/skills/` and
`.ponytail/state`, so nothing else has to move. Leaving both layers on would show
the rules twice.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Discovery and listing：DSH has no first-party plugin registry: `dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the
profile, so npm *is* the distribution channel. The community catalog is
[DSH Plugin Hub](https://dsh-plugin.org), which indexes plugins by the npm keyword
`dsh-plugin` and the GitHub topic `dsh-plugin`.

- npm: `npm search dsh-plugin`
- from inside an agent: install `dsh-find-plugin` and search the `dsh-plugin` topic
- in the GUI: `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin` adds a plugin marketplace
  to Settings

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Discovery and listing：To list a plugin: publish to npm with the `dsh-plugin` keyword, give the repository
the `dsh-plugin` topic, then submit it at <https://dsh-plugin.org> for review.

dsh-plugin-ponytail README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test
```

`test/selfcheck.test.mjs` drives the plugin against stubs of the three host
registries, so discovery, level resolution, mode filtering, the skills provider and
the `/ponytail` handler are all exercised without a running harness.
